run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded, search-index-only run (same network constraint as all recent runs). The session's network policy again blocked ALL direct HTTPS egress: WebFetch/DNS failed with ENOTFOUND for every target host tested, including www.tenders.gov.au, data.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au. No tender portal, detail page, feed/API, or tender document could be opened directly, so discovery was limited to the WebSearch tool, which is US-indexed and returned mostly stale (mid-2026) cached snapshots, JavaScript-disabled portal shells, and third-party aggregator pages. Tier 1 (Commonwealth AusTender, NSW buy.nsw, VIC Buying for Victoria, QLD QTenders/supply.qld.gov.au, WA/SA/TAS/NT/ACT) were swept via search; no directly-verifiable NEW open government notice from the last 7 days could be confirmed against a buyer-originated primary source. Tier 2 (councils via VendorPanel/TenderLink, universities/TAFEs, water/energy GBEs, ports/airports, public health/HealthShare) and Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP/Rio Tinto/Woodside/Fortescue, Woolworths/Coles, Qantas, Telstra, EstimateOne) were checked via search; all corporate channels remained login/registration-gated with no publicly-visible open RFx. Several promising leads surfaced but could not be captured responsibly: a Home Affairs 'JRAS' panel lead resolved to a mis-dated 2007 notice; a Defence Land 6504 item is market research, not an RFT; DFAT-1039 (PNG ESIP 2) is shortlisted/invitation-only (out of scope); and a Tasmanian Government 13-site greenfield aged-care EOI had already closed (6 Nov 2026). Only two buyer-originated opportunities could be carried responsibly this run, both headline-level: ACARA RFT 8-26 (Website Development Services, closing today 9 Nov 2026) and the DTA Digital Marketplace Panel 2 (BuyICT) application channel. One genuinely new buyer-originated council source (Shire of Northam, WA) was identified and verified as absent from the existing 504-source set.
gaps: CRITICAL ACCESS LIMITATION (repeat of every recent run): the session's network policy blocked all direct HTTPS egress and WebFetch. DNS did not resolve (ENOTFOUND) for www.tenders.gov.au, data.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au on direct test, meaning tender hosts are outside the session's allowed network domains. No tender portal, feed/API, detail page or tender document could be opened directly. Hosts needing allow-listing include www.tenders.gov.au (and its data.gov.au 'AusTender Open Approaches to Market' export), www.tenders.nsw.gov.au / buy.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au / supply.qld.gov.au, www.tenders.wa.gov.au, www.tenders.sa.gov.au, www.tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, portal.tenderlink.com, service.ariba.com, estimateone.com, buyict.gov.au, healthsharevic.org.au, watercorporation.com.au and acara.edu.au.

Because direct access was blocked, ALL discovery was via the WebSearch tool only. Both captured entries are headline-level: deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, documents and contacts could not be extracted from source documents and are null. They need a deliverables/detail pass on the live buyer portal once network access is available.

The web-search index was heavily skewed to stale/cached snapshots (mostly mid-2026) and to paid aggregators (australiantenders.com.au, bidsfactory.com, projectory.com.au, tendersontime.com). Live portal pages returned JavaScript-disabled shells with no listing content. Very few opportunities could be confirmed as open or published in the last 7 days from a buyer-originated source.

AusTender (Commonwealth): no confirmable NEW November-2026 ATM could be verified against the primary source; search returned 2024-2025 ATM examples and aggregator rows. A 'HOMEAFFAIRS/2195/RFT JRAS panel closing 17 Nov 2026' lead appeared via an aggregator but could NOT be corroborated - the only matching AusTender notice was a closed 2007 JRAS panel - so it was NOT captured (no fabrication). Federal coverage remains a gap this run, deferred to a future run with portal access.

Defence/CASG: the closest November item (Project Land 6504, published 13 Oct 2026) is market research / an RFI with capability statements due 5 Nov 2026, not an open RFT; not captured. DFAT-1039 (PNG Economic and Social Infrastructure Program ESIP 2, closing ~18 Nov 2026) is released only to shortlisted organisations - invitation-only and OUT OF SCOPE.

Tenders SA, Tenders WA, Tenders Tasmania, QTOL (NT), ACT Tenders: search again returned stale/closed items or South African ('SA') noise; no confirmable open state RFT within the 7-day window. State coverage is a gap this run, deferred.

LEAD for a future run (buyer-originated, could not be captured this run): Tasmanian Government offered 13 government-owned greenfield sites to aged-care/assisted-living providers via an EOI that opened 26 Sep 2026 and CLOSED 6 Nov 2026 - now closed, so out of the open window and not captured. Also City of Sydney 'build and run an affordable residential aged care facility in Redfern' EOI (cityofsydney.nsw.gov.au/opportunities) surfaced but with no verifiable current closing date. Verify both on their buyer portals once access is available.

Tier 3 corporate (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside, Woolworths/Coles, Qantas, Telstra, EstimateOne) mandatory check completed via search: no publicly-visible open RFx found; all are login/registration-gated. Portals already recorded in the known source set (access_method=portal-registration). Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope and were not fabricated.

Tier 2 councils/utilities/ports/health: a wide sample was checked via search (Canada Bay, Tamworth, Wollongong, Central Coast, Gunnedah, Lachlan, Cloncurry, Gold Coast councils; Water Corporation WA, South East Water, Greater Western Water; Pilbara/Southern/Gladstone ports; HealthShare Victoria). All were already in the 504-source aggregate and showed only closed/older opportunities via search; none could be confirmed as currently open. Deferred to a future run with portal access.

Source discovery is approaching saturation on the free-search channel: the known-source aggregate already holds 504 buyer-originated sources, so most council/utility/port candidates surfaced this run were already recorded. Only Shire of Northam (WA) was genuinely new. Finding further new sources will increasingly require authenticated portal crawls rather than web search.
recommended_seed_additions: Shire of Northam (WA) - Tenders & Procurement (own portal at northam.wa.gov.au/tenders + VendorPanel for enquiries) - buyer-originated council source, not previously in the known 504-source set.

Tasmanian Government greenfield aged-care sites EOI process (lead) - a recurring state-government EOI channel for aged-care/assisted-living development; the 2026 round closed 6 Nov 2026. Worth monitoring for the next round via Tenders Tasmania / health.tas.gov.au.

City of Sydney - Opportunities (cityofsydney.nsw.gov.au/opportunities) as a buyer-originated EOI channel distinct from the council's routine procurement portal - confirm and record on a run with portal access.

tenders.description: ACARA is seeking a supplier to provide website development services. The opportunity is published on ACARA's own tenders page with a closing date of Monday 9 November 2026, 3pm (Sydney time).
tenders.submission_method: Via ACARA tender process as described on the ACARA tenders page
tenders.reasoning: Surfaced again via WebSearch against ACARA's own tenders page (acara.edu.au/about-us/tenders), which lists a closing date of Monday 9 November 2026, 3pm Sydney time for Website Development Services. Buyer-originated source. Carried forward from the 2026-11-07 / 2026-11-08 runs; today (9 Nov) is its closing day, so it is closing-soon/closing today.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only: direct portal/document access was blocked this run (ENOTFOUND for acara.edu.au), so deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, value and contacts could not be extracted and are null. Closing date/time confirmed from ACARA's own tenders page listing as re-surfaced in search. Distinct from ACARA's NAP-ICTL 2028 RFT (RFT 5-26), which is invitation-only and out of scope.

tenders.title: Digital Marketplace Panel 2 (DMP2) - reopening for new seller applications (Software and Cloud)
tenders.category: ICT panel / prequalification (digital, software, cloud services)
tenders.description: The DTA's Digital Marketplace Panel 2 (DMP2) is open for new seller applications, including under the Software and Cloud module. Existing sellers on the expiring Software and ERP Marketplace and Cloud Marketplace arrangements are expected to re-apply to DMP2 to continue selling to government.
tenders.eligibility: Open to ICT sellers applying to join the panel (new applicants and existing sellers re-applying); application is via a free BuyICT.gov.au seller account.
tenders.briefing: An industry briefing was referenced in prior reporting but the date could not be confirmed for the current window.
tenders.submission_method: Apply online via BuyICT.gov.au (DTA Digital Marketplace Panel 2)
tenders.reasoning: Buyer-originated federal ICT panel (DTA/BuyICT), carried forward from the 2026-11-08 run as a standing application channel. DMP2 is a recurring panel that reopens for seller applications periodically; pivoted from trade reporting to the DTA/BuyICT source of truth.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only; buyict.gov.au and DTA pages could not be opened directly this run (network egress blocked). The exact current application window (open date, closing date, industry-briefing date) could NOT be confirmed via search and is left null/unverified. Verify the current window on buyict.gov.au before relying on dates.
